Хмф.{E108:0010} А почему же?{E108:0010}
Что именно не так в моём заявлении?

entries.en:
For one thing,{E108:0008} {E1D1}{E188:00310000}the fact that you clearly do not believe
it yourself.
entries.ru: Хотя бы то,{E108:0008} {E1D1}{E188:00310000}что вы и сами в него явно не верите.

entries.en:
Nnghoooh!{E108:0018}
(Was it that obvious?)
entries.ru:
Нгхооо!{E108:0018}
(Неужели так заметно?)

entries.en: (I'm going to have to be more careful next time.)
entries.ru: (В следующий раз надо быть осторожнее.)

entries.en:
Would you care to revise your testimony at all, Judge
Gavèlle?
entries.ru:
Не желаете ли что-нибудь исправить в показаниях,
судья Молотова?

entries.en:
No,{E108:0008} why?{E108:0010} Do you believe there is something wrong
with it?

Then perhaps...{E108:0010} {E1D1}{E188:00310000}{E12F:00080007}you could refrain from insinuating
otherwise?
entries.ru:
Тогда, быть может...{E108:0010} {E1D1}{E188:00310000}{E12F:00080007}воздержитесь от намёков
на обратное?

entries.en:
Nngh!{E108:0018}
(Well that blew up in my face...)
entries.ru:
Нгх!{E108:0018}
(Что ж, это вышло мне боком...)

entries.en:
I'm afraid there is still one question concerning the
IS-7 Incident that remains unanswered, Your Honor.
...Would you mind taking a look at this?
What is it...?

They're test results,{E108:0008} carried out on the liquid at the
bottom of the Gemini case in the Winter Wing.
As you can see,{E108:0008} traces of blood were detected.
The question is,{E108:0010} whose?

Until that question is answered,{E108:0010} {E188:00200000}{E1DA}{E1D5}I hardly think you can
claim to have "all the evidence"!
There was blood in the Gemini case...?
Why did I not hear about this from Eustace?

Because Detective Gumshoe informed me of the
results directly.

...I was planning to tell Mr. Winner about it myself, of
course.

You...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E282}You kept this to yourself until now!?{E108:0010}
Despite having no jurisdiction here whatsoever!?

Mark my words.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1DA}{E1D5}{E188:00200000}The Committee will hear all about
what you have done here today.

As ever,{E108:0008} my interest is in the truth.{E108:0010} And if mistakes
were made in the past,{E108:0008} they must be rectified.
If you must report me to the Committee,{E108:0008} {E1D5}{E1D1}then so be it.

But in return,{E108:0008} we must be allowed to investigate this
case to the very end!
...That is not my decision to make.
You will need to discuss it with Eustace.
Guess who's back, losers!{E108:0018} And with good news, too!

It was a close call for a minute there, but...{E108:0010} Carmelo
Gusto is alive!
Gusto...!
You're the ones who found me?

Yup.{E108:0018}
...Long time no see, Gusto.

You've grown!{E108:0018} And you have an assistant of your own
now?

Heh heh!{E108:0010} He hasn't got the gig just yet.{E108:0010}
This is Gregory Edgeworth's son.
...Prosecutor Miles Edgeworth,{E108:000C} at your service.
Hngh.{E108:0010} {E1D1}Fate moves in mysterious ways...!

I'm in your debt!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}If you hadn't found me in time,{E108:0008}
I wouldn't be here to thank you.
Oh...{E108:0008} {E107:0002}you're very welcome.

After all,{E108:0008} if you hadn't lived,{E108:0008} {E1D5}we wouldn't be able to ask
you what really happened eighteen years ago.

Hrngh...?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}What are you talking about?
We figured out quite a bit while you were out cold.

Including the fact that you're probably the guy who
offed poor Artie Frost.
Whaaat!?{E108:0018} Is that true!?

Ms. Bound set up a very elaborate trap to catch
Mr. Frost's murderer.

...A trap that involved rigging the Pisces case with
poison gas.
Perhaps in light of that fact...

...you could tell us in your own words what happened
back then?

...Or perhaps you'd rather exercise your right to
remain silent?

Oh,{E108:0008} it's not that.{E108:0010} Gusto here's a fan of the ol'
meditation.{E108:0010} You know,{E108:0008} "om" and all that jazz.

Wow,{E108:0008} sleeping while standing seems pretty cool!{E108:0010}
{E1D9}That's one heck of a talent!

(Except there's no sleeping involved in meditation,
Kay...)

Hey!{E108:0010} Gusto, old pal!{E108:0018} How about you snap out of it and
tell us what went down way back when!

I was caught in the girl's trap,{E108:0008} so I must be the killer...?{E108:0018}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}{E12F:00200004}...Is this your idea of a joke?
I'm the victim here!

Indeed you are, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} And there is no evidence
that you have done anything wrong yet.
Mr. Edgeworth and Mr. Fender are merely speculating.

Rest assured that they have no authority here,{E108:0008} {E1D1}and
that you may pay them no heed.

Hngh...!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}At least somebody here seems to be on my
side.
Judge Verity Gavèlle.{E108:0010} It's a pleasure, Mr. Gusto.
I will assist you in any way you may require.

Perhaps you could begin by explaining what actually
happened eighteen years ago to Mr. Edgeworth?
Hrngh...{E108:0018} Fine.

You want me to prove I'm innocent, Mr. Prosecutor?{E108:0010}
{E282}I'll be happy to.
So this is how you mean to play it,{E108:0018} {E107:0003}Judge Gavèlle?

You're hoping Mr. Gusto will help you to hide what
happened instead of trying to correct the record!?

...I believe only in the infallible judgment of the
Goddess of Justice.

Except it is us humans who make the actual judgment
calls in a court of law.

And so long as there are those who would use the law
to their advantage,{E108:0008} our rulings are fallible indeed.

If you would use your position to further obscure the
truth...{E108:0018} {E107:0003}{E1D1}then neither she nor I will forgive you.
Hah hah...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}We shall see about that.
What do you advise, Judge Gavèlle?

It would seem that you are under suspicion because it
was you who triggered the poison gas.
Specifically,{E108:0008} by opening the Pisces case's lid.
Would you be so kind as to share why with us?
Understood.
I came to see Frost's sculptures.{E108:0010} Simple as that.

I made a mistake with the opening times,{E108:0008} and arrived
a half hour early.

Ms. Bound,{E108:0010} was there no one at the reception desk at
around that time?

I had left the main entrance unguarded and unlocked,{E108:0008}
just in case the killer made an appearance.

I was also busy making preparations elsewhere,{E108:0008} all the
way up until the gallery's opening.
So no,{E108:0008} there was no one here on the first floor then.

But...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E285}I did make sure that all the wings were locked up
tight --{E108:0010} all except for the Autumn Wing, that is.
...I see.
entries.ru: ...Понятно.

entries.en:
(She did all that just to steer the culprit into the
Autumn Wing...)
(Which is precisely where Mr. Gusto went.)

Sneaking into a building's pretty suspicious,{E108:0008} however
you slice it...
Silence in the courtroom!

I will permit no objections or interventions unless
there is {E1D1}some evidence that the witness is lying.

The courtroom!?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}You know this is an art gallery, right?

Mr. Gusto,{E108:0018} {E12F:0008000E}{E112:0008}{E12F:0008000F}{E107:0002}if you could please continue by explaining
why you opened the Pisces case.
I wanted to see Frost's work up close.

So I went up to the Gemini--{E108:0010} sorry,{E108:0008} {E284}guess it was
supposed to be the Pisces statue...

...and I saw that the lid was frozen on tight.{E108:0010} So I
grabbed a blowtorch from nearby and tried to open it.
When I finally got it open,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E1D9}gas came pouring out.

Fascinating.{E108:0018} {E107:0002}His is the sort of flawless testimony
attorneys can only dream of.
Yeah.{E108:0010} The {E1D1}"everything sounds like a lie" kind.

I am none too satisfied with Mr. Gusto's explanation
myself.
Alas...{E108:0010} {E285}{E107:0002}there is no evidence to refute it.
Come on!{E108:0010} There must be something...!
It's Bound's story you should be questioning,{E108:0008} {E1D1}not mine!

I'm not the one who set up the gas trap!{E108:0010}
She could have killed anybody with that thing!

She turned on the sprinklers as soon as the gas was
released.

She knew exactly what she was doing.{E108:0010}
{E1D1}She was gunning for the killer,{E108:0008} and nobody else.
...That killer being you,{E108:0010} old pal.
So you...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}believe that self-confessed criminal?

Ms. Bound is far from blameless in this affair.{E108:0010}
And she will have to pay for her crimes.
But so will Mr. Frost's killer.
You seem determined to pin Frost's murder on me.
But I had no reason to kill him.
And you have no evidence to prove otherwise!
Gnrk!
entries.ru: Гнрх!

entries.en:
Can we really not prove that he's the killer,
{E1D1}Mr. Edgeworth?

Mr. Gusto fell victim to the poison gas.{E108:0010}
That much is indisputable...

Yet, no matter how suspicious his actions in the
present may seem,{E108:0008} they prove nothing about the past.

Yeah, but...!{E108:0020} {E12F:00020001}{E107:0002}Then what about you, Mr. Fender?{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}There must be something we can do!

You're right...{E108:0010} We may not have evidence,{E108:0008} {E188:00300000}{E1D5}but we
have plenty of intel.{E108:0018} {E107:0003}Let's see now...
If Gusto killed Frost,{E108:0008} he must have had a reason.

In fact,{E108:0008} your old man had a little back and forth with
von Karma about a probable motive, too, remember?
How can you possibly say that with any certainty?
entries.ru: Как вы можете утверждать это с уверенностью?

entries.en:
If {E043}their relationship had {E188:002F0000}{E1D5}broken down{E040} for some
reason...{E106}{E198:00020029}{E100:0001}{E1AE}{E12D:00030882}{E100:0000}{E12F:00050005}{E101:00050005}{E107:0001}{E188:00200000}{E1D2}{E1D5}...that could very well have been the motive behind
this murder!

Von Karma wouldn't let us talk to Gusto back then.{E108:0010}
But we can now.

If we can put the pieces together...{E108:0008} I think the picture
we've been looking for might just emerge.
Yes...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I think you might be right.

(I need to think back over everything we know about
the IS-7 Incident.)
(Especially the questions that never got answered...!)

And the finger marks...?{E108:0010}
{E1D1}{E284}...Were you the one wearing the gloves?
entries.ru:
А следы пальцев...?{E108:0010}
{E1D1}{E284}...Это вы были в перчатках?

entries.en:
(Ms. Scone denied that the finger marks on the frame
were hers.)
(But what if they were Mr. Gusto's?)

(Perhaps he had wanted to take a look through the
{E043}ultimate cookbook{E042} for himself...)
So he asked me to go put in a new cartridge.
entries.ru: И он попросил меня вставить новую кассету.

entries.en:
He seemed to think there should have been more shots
left than there were...
entries.ru:
Ему казалось, что кадров должно было остаться
больше...

entries.en:
In other words,{E108:0008} the film ran out sooner than
expected?
entries.ru:
Иначе говоря,{E108:0008} плёнка кончилась раньше,
чем ожидалось?

entries.en:
Yes.{E108:0008} The number of shots he took didn't line up with
the number of shots remaining.{E106}{E198:0002002A}{E100:0001}{E1AE}{E12D:00030885}{E100:0000}{E101:001D001E}{E107:0003}But...{E108:0008} {E107:0002}he thought maybe he'd just lost track somewhere
along the way.

(My father noticed these things for a reason.{E108:0010}
I just need to piece them together correctly.)

(In the absence of evidence,{E108:0008} {E1D1}it's the only way to the
truth!)

Eighteen years ago,{E108:0008} Mr. Gusto and Mr. Frost
collaborated in the confectionery contest.

But why did they work together,{E108:0008} and why did they
enter the contest in the first place?

That's the information I need to get out of my
opponent somehow.

(Hmm...{E108:0010} Mr. Gusto seems to have a habit of {E188:00300000}{E1D5}{E041}pretending
to be asleep{E042} when things aren't going his way...)

Let's start by focusing on {E284}{E043}why he chose to work with
Mr. Frost{E040}.

By my hand,{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E283}{E173:0001}now is the time to dig up the truth that
was buried all those years ago!

Mr. Gusto,{E108:0010} what inspired you to collaborate with
Mr. Frost?
We were acquaintances before we were contestants.

He was interested in entering the contest,{E108:0008} so we
decided to sign up together.

Heh...{E108:0010} And your decision to pair up with a sculptor had
nothing to do with your lack of faith in your skills?
Hrngh...!{E108:0010} {E1D1}You don't know me!

We joined forces because {E1D1}{E281}we wanted to make the most
perfect creations possible!{E108:0010} That's all!

I will expose all your lies in the end, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010}
It's only a matter of time.

Hngh...{E108:0008} Sorry.{E108:0010} Wanted to see if I could do an
impression of you.{E108:0010} Turns out it's easy.

(Ngrk...{E108:0010} {E1D1}He's happy to bide his time as well it seems.{E108:0010}
I'll need to pick my words more wisely.)
Frost's son and mine were in the same grade at school.
So we got along pretty well, too.

Oh?{E108:0018} So you were just two friends who happened to try
for the title of "world's greatest confectioner"?

Heh...{E108:0010} Pretending to be asleep when the going gets
tough won't work on me, I'm afraid.
Mr. Frost was a sculptor, Mr. Gusto.

I doubt he cared much about winning a title for
confectioners.

In which case,{E108:0008} {E1D1}he probably had a different motive for
taking part in the contest,{E108:0008} wouldn't you say?
Fine...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}It was me.{E108:0010} I wanted that title.

Frost was only in it for the prize --{E108:0008} the ultimate
cookbook.

I see.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}And since your objectives dovetailed so neatly,{E108:0008}
you decided to work together.

But then,{E108:0008} something happened.{E108:0010} A breakdown in your
relationship, perhaps?{E108:0010} If so,{E108:0008} I want to know why.

............{E107:0003}Mr. Prosecutor.{E108:0018}
{E1D1}I'm still quite unwell after my brush with death.

Push me too hard...{E108:0010} {E152:002000050001}{E112:0020}and I'll be on my way {E188:00340000}{E1D1}back to the
medical room!

Then you'd better wrap this up quickly.{E108:0010}
{E12F:00200004}I'm already {E188:00340000}{E1D1}dangerously low on patience.

...Mr. Gusto is trying desperately to make his escape.{E108:0010}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}But he's not going anywhere yet.

Not as long as he's still keeping things from me.{E108:0010}
So let's figure out {E284}{E043}what he was really after{E040} next.

There's no time to lose.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}{E282}{E173:0000}I need to pick the right line of
questioning,{E108:0008} {E1D2}and fast!

You wanted to appear on Mr. Tangaroa's TV show,
didn't you?
(...I believe it was called{E108:0008} {E188:00300000}{E1D5}"Bake 'n' Bop"...?)

You really think people would've wanted to watch me
{E1D1}dance like an idiot while I work?

N-No...{E108:0010} {E1D1}It might have been a bit much for younger
viewers...
Hrngh!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I thought not.

Listen,{E108:0010} I know what I'm good at.{E108:0018}
And prancing around on TV isn't it!

Maybe you should focus on what you're good at, too.{E108:0010}
{E188:00310000}{E1D1}'Cause it certainly isn't asking the right questions!

Nnrgh...!{E108:0010} Touché, Mr. Gusto...{E108:0010}
(I need to choose my words more carefully.)

You too had your eyes on something other than the
title, didn't you?

After all,{E108:0008} I'm not sure the title of "world's greatest
confectioner" even counts for that much.

Hrnnnnnngh...!?{E108:0018} {E107:0001}{E188:00310000}{E1D1}{E12F:00200004}Now you're insulting the way of the
confectioner!?

My goal --{E108:0008} my only goal --{E108:0010} {E1D1}was to win that title!{E108:0018}
{E107:0001}{E281}I didn't care about anything else!
You have no idea {E283}how much it would've meant to me!

Look,{E108:0008} my sense of design may not have been up to
snuff back then,{E108:0010} but you should see me now!
Oh?{E108:0018} So you've improved?

You bet I have!{E108:0018} {E1D1}I didn't do all that training in Zheng Fa
for nothing!

I looked up to Tangaroa, you know.{E108:0010} Spent hours
poring over the designs of his work.
Even used to watch his show with my son.

Sounds to me like Mr. Tangaroa's work {E188:002F0000}was especially
influential in your early studies.

And with his recipe book,{E108:0008} {E1D1}you might have even
become the best someday.

The book was a real treasure,{E108:0008} no doubt about that.{E108:0010}
{E1D1}Any confectioner would have wanted it.

Heh.{E108:0018} You claim that your only goal was to win the
title...

...yet you also seem to have had an interest in the
contest's prize, the ultimate cookbook.

Hnnnnnngggrrrrrrh!{E108:0028}{E12F:00200000} {E1D2}The greatest collection of recipes
by the world's greatest confectionier...
I can't say I had absolutely no interest in it.........!
And even if I did,{E12F:00200005}{E112:0020}{E108:0008} {E12F:00200004}{E1D2}what exactly is so {E188:00360000}wrong with that!?
...Nothing, I suppose.

(Only that the book contained {E188:00300000}recipes for medicines,{E108:0008}
not desserts...)

(And everyone who entered the contest supposedly
knew that.)
...Hrrrnnngh!

I feel like I'm finally getting somewhere.{E108:0010}
I can't let him slip from my grasp now!
I just need to {E1D1}stay calm{E108:0008} and {E1D1}keep the pressure on.
Next,{E108:0008} let's find out {E283}{E173:0000}{E043}why he wanted the cookbook{E040}!

So your plan was to win the cookbook{E108:0008} {E188:00300000}and use it to
help you with your own creations?

What else?{E108:0010} A book like that could have improved my
craft tenfold.
You could have made a lot of money {E108:0008}{E1D1}if you'd sold it...

Hngh.........{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I don't know much about what was actually
{E1D1}in there...
...but it was {E1D1}worth more than money,{E108:0008} {E1D1}I'll tell you that.

Come now, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} I think you know more about
the ultimate cookbook than you claim.

Hrngh...{E108:0010} They told us a little about it at the start of the
contest.

Heh...{E108:0010} Then you know what kind of recipes it actually
contained, don't you?
And that they weren't dessert recipes at all!
Hrrrnnnnnnnnngh!

I see you did your homework.{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}Fine,{E108:0008} so you know what was really in there.

The ultimate cookbook...{E108:0008} or the "Angel's Cookbook",{E108:0008} to
give it its proper title.

It's a collection of chemical formulas and ways to
synthesize new medicines {E188:00340000}{E1D1}nobody had ever heard of.

So he did know that {E043}the cookbook actually contained
recipes for medicines{E040}.
This could be {E285}an important {E041}clue{E040}.
Did you know how valuable the cookbook really was?

What kind of question is that!?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}It was a collection of Tangaroa's recipes!

There wasn't a confectioner in the world who wouldn't
have wanted to get their hands on it!

I don't have a {E041}clue{E040} as to how to proceed with this line
of questioning.
entries.ru:
У меня нет {E041}зацепки{E040}, чтобы продолжать допрос
в этом направлении.

entries.en: ...I'd better try another tack.
Time to deploy {E285}my {E041}clue{E040}...

Your designs may have improved thanks to your
training in Zheng Fa...

...but you clearly didn't do enough work on your skills
of deception.

You've already admitted that you knew the ultimate
cookbook was a collection of recipes for medicines!

Thereby making your interest not gastronomical,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}but
pharmaceutical in nature!

You're a confectioner, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} You had no
professional interest in revolutionary new medicines.

Which suggests{E108:0008} {E188:00200000}{E1D2}that your interest must have been
personal.
Hrrrrrrnnnnnngaaah!
Nngh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}I underestimated you.

Fine...{E108:0010} You're right.{E112:0020}{E108:0010} {E188:00340000}{E1D1}Winning the title wasn't the only
reason I entered the contest.

I needed one of the recipes in that book.{E108:0010}
...It was for my son.{E108:0010} He was sick.

.........{E107:0002}{E1D1}That's none of your business.{E108:0010} {E1D1}I've told you as
much as you need to know.

(Hmm.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E188:00300000}He looks {E041}rattled{E042}.{E108:0010} But I can't let him off the
hook.)
Let's find out {E108:0008}{E284}{E043}what this mystery illness was{E040}.

I've almost gotten to the bottom of this,{E108:0008} I can feel it!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}Just a few more moves...!
Tell me a little more about your son.
He was my pride and joy.{E108:0010} And my biggest fan.
And you entered the contest in order to help him?

You clearly don't have children of your own.{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}Any father would have done the same!

I would have done anything to help him!{E108:0010}
{E1D2}Anything!

He would come see me here at the contest venue,
too --{E108:0010} right up through the semifinal.
Really?{E108:0010} He didn't get in the way of your work?

If you were trying to beat Samson Tangaroa,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}surely
you didn't have the time to look after a child!
Yeah, well...{E108:0010} I wanted to do what I could for him.

He said he wanted to always be {E1D1}the first to try my
creations...
You said your son was sick, Mr. Gusto...

And yet he was able to come and join you for the
contest?
Hngh...!

It wasn't...{E108:0008} that kind of illness.{E108:0010}
{E284}Nothing life-threatening, anyway...
(Hmm...{E108:0010} This feels like it could be {E285}an important {E041}clue{E042}...)
So you needed the cookbook to cure your son?

...Yeah.{E108:0010} Nowadays,{E108:0008} you can get the medication he
needed anywhere.
But back then,{E108:0008} {E1D1}that book was our only hope.

Which is why I didn't dare waste my time on fancy tea
parties!{E108:0010} {E1D1}I had to give my all to my work!
And what about Mr. Tangaroa's work?

Surely that tea break gave you the perfect opportunity
to go steal a glance at it?

.........{E107:0002}{E1D1}And what makes you think I had the {E1D1}energy or
time to care about what {E1D1}the others had made...?

I think you've made it abundantly clear how much
interest you had in Mr. Tangaroa's work.

What's more,{E108:0008} if you were that determined to win the
ultimate cookbook...

...I seriously doubt you would've passed up on a
chance to take a peek at your competitors' entries!
...Hrngh...{E108:0010} {E1D2}Hrnnnnnnnnngh.

I'd had plenty of chances throughout the contest to see
and sample my rivals' work, you know.

But each time I did...{E108:0010} {E152:002000050001}{E112:0020}{E284}nothing seemed to have any
flavor.
Must have been...{E108:0008} {E107:0002}nerves or something...
(Nothing Mr. Gusto tasted {E043}had any flavor{E042}...?)
(That seems like it could be {E285}an important {E041}clue{E042}...)

Could you tell me the name of the disease your son
suffered from?
Hrngh...{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E188:00310000}{E1D1}{E12F:00200004}You're a real cold customer, Mr. Prosecutor!

Isn't it enough that he was seriously ill?{E108:0018}
{E283}Why would you force me to tell you more!?

I don't have a {E041}clue{E040} as to how to proceed with this line
of questioning.
entries.ru:
У меня нет {E041}зацепки{E040}, чтобы продолжать допрос
в этом направлении.

entries.en: ...I'd better try another tack.
Time to deploy {E285}my {E041}clue{E040}...

You've already shared with me that your son's illness
wasn't life-threatening.

So why are you so reluctant to share any further
details?

It may not have been life-threatening,{E108:0008} but that doesn't
mean it hadn't been life-altering.
I see.{E108:0010} That must have been {E1D1}very hard on both of you.

Of course it was.{E108:0010}
{E1D1}That was why I did everything I could to find a cure.
We were desperate.

He couldn't taste anything.{E108:0010}
Not even his favorite desserts...

As I understand it,{E108:0008} the ultimate cookbook contains the
recipe for a very particular medication.

One that Mr. Tangaroa used to cure himself of his own
{E285}taste disorder.
So your son has a taste disorder then,{E108:0008} am I correct?
Hrrrnnn{E1D2}ghhhah!{E108:0018}{E112:0020} {E12F:00200003}How did I let that slip!?

You've been asking me to believe that you {E1D1}needed to
win the cookbook in order to cure your son.
But was that really the case?

............{E108:0010}
{E107:0002}Hrngh!{E108:0010} Of course it was!{E108:0010} {E1D1}What are you saying!?

I'm saying that I'm not so sure that's true based on
everything you've told me.

I don't have a {E041}clue{E040} as to how to proceed with this line
of questioning.
entries.ru:
У меня нет {E041}зацепки{E040}, чтобы продолжать допрос
в этом направлении.

entries.en: ...I'd better try another tack.
Time to deploy {E285}my {E041}clue{E040}...

Taste disorders are difficult to live with.{E108:0010} {E12F:00000008}It isn't easy
not being able to enjoy your food.

You should know.{E108:0010} After all,{E108:0008} you just told me you'd
experienced something like that during the contest.

You said that nothing you sampled had any flavor.{E108:0010}
Those were your words, correct?

Which would seem to suggest that {E284}you were suffering
from a taste disorder.

A confectioner without a sense of taste?{E108:0010}
Not exactly ideal.

Are you sure it wasn't actually your own condition you
were seeking a cure for, Mr. Gusto?

Hrrrnnn{E1D2}gggrrr!{E108:0018}
{E107:0003}{E1D1}I've had enough of your speculations!

I managed just fine in that contest!{E108:0010}
{E1D1}Made all my own entries,{E108:0008} {E1D1}no problems!

Heh...{E108:0010} Sorry,{E108:0008} but I'm afraid you're contradicting your
own testimony.

You already admitted that you and Mr. Frost had
worked together during the contest!
It's too late to claim you did it all on your own now!

You would have us believe that you are a man of
principle.{E108:0010} A dedicated student of the confectioner's art.

Yet you abandoned those principles and conspired
with Mr. Frost to rig the contest.
All so you could cure{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E188:00200000}{E1D2}{E1D5}{E112:0000}{E12F:0000000D}your own taste disorder!
.........{E108:0008}{E107:0003}You got me, Mr. Prosecutor.
As you said,{E108:0008} {E12F:00200004}my sense of taste was shot.

I'd kept it hidden for so long...{E108:0010}
{E1D1}Eighteen years{E108:0008} {E1D1}{E188:002F0000}and nobody knew...!
Sadly,{E108:0008} you can lie to others,{E108:0008} {E285}but you can't lie to me.

Both Mr. Gusto and Mr. Frost entered the contest
hoping to obtain the ultimate cookbook.

For {E1D1}the medicine that would cure Mr. Gusto's disorder,{E108:0010}
and {E1D1}the money it would bring in for Mr. Frost.
Thus, an uneasy alliance was forged.

I need to study my opponent's reactions,{E108:0008} and pick my
own responses accordingly.

Hrrrngh...{E108:0010} I'm still recovering,{E108:0008} so if you've got nothing
to say,{E108:0008} let me go back to the medical room.

W-Wait...!{E108:0018}
(I may need to be a little more proactive...)

I've exhausted this avenue of enquiry.{E108:0010}
Let me try another angle.
entries.ru:
Эта линия допроса исчерпана.{E108:0010}
Попробую зайти с другой стороны.

entries.en:
.........{E107:0002}I think it's about time we took a break from all
this questioning,{E108:0008} don't you?
C-Curses...
entries.ru: П-Проклятье...

entries.en: I can't give up now.{E108:0010} I have to keep pushing...
entries.ru: Сдаваться нельзя.{E108:0010} Нужно давить дальше...

entries.en: Alright...{E108:0018} {E283}Once more unto the breach!
entries.ru: Что ж...{E108:0018} {E283}Идём на новый приступ!

entries.en: Hrrrrrrnngaahhh!

I'll admit it...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}You're good.{E108:0010} I never told anybody any of
this,{E108:0008} but you figured it all out anyway.
It's true.{E108:0010} Eighteen years ago,{E108:0008} {E188:00300000}{E1D5}I developed {E041}ageusia{E040}.

It's a taste disorder that makes it so you can't taste
anything at all.
A confectioner's worst nightmare.
Mr. Fender.{E108:0010} Is this what Mr. Tangaroa had as well?

No.{E108:0010} The big man had what they call {E285}{E041}dissociated taste
disorder{E040}.

Basically,{E108:0008} some things he could taste just fine,{E108:0008} while
others had no flavor at all.
So he suffered, too.{E108:0010} Can't have been easy.
Not when there wasn't a way to cure it on the market.
Which is why you needed Mr. Tangaroa's cookbook.

Do you admit now that that was the real reason you
entered the contest?

It was only one of the reasons.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}I wasn't lying when
I said I wanted the title.

When I put my mind to something,{E108:0008} it gets done!{E108:0018}
And I won't lose to anybody!

I may not have been able to taste it then,{E108:0008} but I still
knew my stuff was good enough to win!

Oh?{E108:0018} So you went into the final thinking you stood a
good chance of winning?

(What was it that Fender said about what
Mr. Tangaroa thought of Mr. Gusto's creations...?)

Mr. Gusto's creations were a perfect balance of flavor
and design.{E108:0010} At least,{E108:0008} up through the semifinal.
entries.ru:
У мистера Густо вкус и форма были в идеальном
равновесии.{E108:0010} По крайней мере{E108:0008} до полуфинала.

entries.en:
But, disappointingly,{E108:0008} his entry for the final was
sub-par on {E1D1}both counts.
entries.ru:
Но, к разочарованию,{E108:0008} его финальная работа
оказалась слабой по {E1D1}обеим статьям.

entries.en:
We were told that your entry for the final was far from
the prize-winning taste sensation you describe.

What happened, Mr. Gusto?{E108:0010}
What went wrong that day?

You want me to talk,{E108:0010} I'll talk!{E108:0018}
{E1D1}But you're not going to like what I have to say!
-- My Entry for the Final --

Frost and I were working together right up through the
semifinal.{E108:0010} I handled the flavor,{E108:0008} he did the designing.

But I wanted to face Tangaroa in the final on my own.{E108:0010}
No help.{E108:0010} Just me and my skills.
So I helped Frost with his entry,{E108:0010} but mine,{E108:0008} {E1D1}I did alone.

If it didn't taste good in the final,{E108:0008} that's on me.{E108:0010}
What can I say?{E108:0010} I lacked training.
And that's all there is to it.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E280}Happy now?

Arngh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}There don't seem to be any obvious
contradictions in his testimony...!

Yep.{E108:0010} {E284}Not that I thought it'd be easy to get anything real
out of him.

He's managed to not let slip what really happened for
eighteen years, after all.

Why don't you try pushing him a bit, Milesarino?{E108:0010}
See if you can't shake something loose?
...I think I just might have to, Fender.
-- My Entry for the Final --

Frost and I were working together right up through the
semifinal. I handled the flavor, he did the designing.

But I wanted to face Tangaroa in the final on my own.
No help. Just me and my skills.
So I helped Frost with his entry, but mine, I did alone.

If it didn't taste good in the final, that's on me.
What can I say? I lacked training.

The only difference between the semifinal and the
final was that Frost wasn't helping me.

My son and Frost's used to go to elementary school
together.
(An eighteen-year-old mystery...)
(And the key to unraveling it{E108:0008} is finally in my grasp.)

(I just need to remember everything Fender told me
about what {E1D1}he and my father discovered...!)

Frost was in charge of designing the work you both
submitted,{E108:0008} while {E285}you handled the taste?

Yeah.{E108:0010} He was a sculptor.{E108:0008} A craftsman.{E108:0010}
And his sense of design was second to none.

But he was {E1D1}clueless about confectionery.{E108:0010} Which is
where I came in.{E108:0010} We each did what the other couldn't.

Heh!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}And boy did you not have an eye for aesthetics!{E108:0010}
Not even for the simple stuff.
Hrngh...!
...How do you like me now?
Huh.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}The national symbol of Zheng Fa.

Oh, yeah!{E108:0010} It's a phoenix!{E108:0018}
{E1D1}That's awesome!

I'll say!{E108:0018} Pretty different to the stuff you were pumping
out eighteen years ago!

Hnnngahahahahaaa!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}Behold the fruits of my training!
I've dedicated my whole life to my craft.

But back then,{E108:0008} we both needed each other's help.{E108:0010}
So we joined hands until the final.
You were serious about winning the title, then?

Of course.{E108:0010} The art of confectionery is my life.{E108:0018} Why
wouldn't I have wanted to be crowned the greatest?

...But I still had a lot to learn back then.{E108:0010}
Guess it's no surprise my work wasn't up to scratch.

But the title wasn't the only thing you wanted.{E108:0010}
{E284}There was the cookbook, too.

And you wanted the book even more than you wanted
the title.{E108:0010} Isn't that right, Mr. Gusto?

Hrngh{E107:0007}............{E108:0018}{E104}{E100:0001}{E1EA:00050027}{E125:0008000C}{E112:0008}{E100:0000}{E12F:0008000C}{E101:00080009}{E107:0002}{E1D1}Mr. Edgeworth,{E108:0010} you are badgering a witness who is
still suffering the effects of today's attack.
I cannot allow this harrassment to continue.
Nnrgh!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}I understand, Your Honor, but...!

Ignore him, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} You need not answer that vile
prosecutor's question!

But please,{E108:0008} do continue your testimony in your own
time.
So you're saying Mr. Frost didn't help you at all...?

But he'd helped you up until then, correct?{E108:0010} It's a bit
strange for him to stop so late in the contest, no?

Strange or not,{E108:0008} it's the truth.{E108:0010} Could be he had his
reasons, too.{E108:0010} I wouldn't know.

If he's lying,{E108:0008} {E1D1}it's going to be a headache to prove.{E108:0010}
Eighteen years is a long time.

Not unless that gizmo of yours has {E188:002F0000}{E1D5}a built-in lie
detector, Kay?

If it did,{E108:0008} I'd have stolen the show from Mr. Edgeworth
long before now!

...Don't worry, Fender.{E108:0010} I can tell when he's lying.{E108:0010}
No doohickey's assistance required.
Please, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} Continue your testimony.

And yet,{E108:0008} I heard that your creations prior to the final
were scored highly for their flavor.

So what went wrong?{E108:0010}
Was there some kind of cooking accident on that day?
Hngh...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E1D1}No.{E108:0010} Nothing like that.
It was...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}I told you --{E108:0008} {E1D5}I had a taste disorder.
My sense of taste failed me.{E108:0010} It's as simple as that.

But Mr. Frost's entry was complimented on its flavor.{E108:0010}
Your sense of taste hadn't failed you then.
Did something happen overnight?

Hmm...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I don't think he's going spill any more beans,
Mr. Edgeworth.
(Then perhaps I should ask him about something else.)
You knew Mr. Frost from before the contest, correct?
Hrngh...{E108:0010} You remembered, I see...
(No,{E108:0008} I'll just stick with what I have for now.)

Did something change between the semifinal and the
final, Mr. Gusto?
Hmm...{E108:0010} Not really...

So you really completed your final entry without
Mr. Frost's help?

I may not have had his designs to lean on, {E108:0008}{E107:0002}{E1D1}but I knew I
was still solid when it came to flavor.

So the visuals were the only thing that changed
between the semifinal and the final.

You sure, Gusty, old pal?{E108:0010} {E1D1}Gonna have to call you out
on that one, I'm afraid.

It wasn't just its looks that got a big thumbs-down
come judgment time.{E108:0010} {E285}It got trashed on {E041}flavor{E040}, too.
Doesn't sound much like a winner to me...

(Despite his confidence,{E108:0008} Mr. Gusto failed on {E041}flavor{E042},
too.)

(The lack of Mr. Frost's assistance shouldn't have
affected that.{E108:0010} {E1D1}So was there some other difference...?)

It was no coincidence that you both entered the
contest, correct?
Yeah.{E108:0010} I heard about it first.{E108:0010} Then I told Frost.

I knew he'd be interested.{E108:0010} {E1D1}He was always short of cash
for his sculptures.

(That's right...{E108:0010} Mr. Frost was supposedly always in
financial trouble, wasn't he?)

The cookbook is really worth that much, huh?{E108:0010}
{E107:0003}Hmm...

I see that glint in your eye, kiddo.{E108:0010} But don't get your
Great Thief-ing hopes up.{E108:0010} It was worth a lot back then.

But these days,{E108:0008} you can find most of the stuff in there
on any drugstore shelf.

(So literally every last contestant only ever had eyes
for that cookbook, I see...)
You're lying, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} And this proves it!

...This is no time for meditation!{E108:0010}
{E1D2}{E188:00310000}I need you to look at the evidence!

Well, I don't need to look at it.{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}It's garbage.{E108:0018} And you need to try harder.
Nnrgh...!
entries.ru: Нгрх...!

entries.en:
If you're looking to improve your professional skills,{E108:0008}
I wholeheartedly recommend going to Zheng Fa.
This evidence will expose the truth at last!
...Pathetic.{E108:0018} Is this your idea of a joke?

(It's not...{E108:0010} but this evidence doesn't point to any kind
of contradiction at all, does it...!?)
May I continue?
There's a contradiction in your testimony, Mr. Gusto.

...Oh?{E108:0010}
You do like to spout some real nonsense, don't you?

You're no match for your father.{E108:0010}
{E107:0003}Not by a long shot.
How dare y--!

Hngeh heh heh heh!{E108:0010}
Too close to home?{E108:0010} My bad.

I can think of one significant difference between the
semifinal and the final, Mr. Gusto.

Your son.{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}This is him in the photograph, correct?

You told me he was here with you up through the
semifinal.

What indeed.{E108:0010} He was here with you until the semifinal,{E108:0008}
until he suddenly wasn't for the final.

And just as suddenly,{E108:0008} your work went from being
lauded for its flavor to being lambasted for it.
I don't think that's a coincidence,{E108:0010} do you?

He wasn't just spending quality time with his father.{E108:0010}
{E188:002F0000}{E1D5}He was playing a much more pivotal role than that.

...I just wanted him to see me hard at work.{E108:0010}
To show him I was trying my best for us.

Who knows?{E108:0010} Maybe it was him being here that helped
me do so well in those early rounds.

He talks a good game,{E108:0008} {E1D1}but nothing about this guy
screams "Superdad" to me...

Indeed.{E108:0010} Thankfully,{E108:0008} we would only have to give such
an idea credence if his story were true.

After all,{E108:0008} how much could the encouragement of one
small boy affect the taste of a grown man's work?

(Mr. Gusto prided himself on the flavor of his
creations,{E108:0008} but then he lost his sense of taste.)

(He must've had a tough time maintaining his high
standards after such a devastating loss,{E108:0008} {E107:0003}unless...)

I'm sure your son was here to cheer you on.{E108:0010}
{E284}But that wasn't all he was here to do, was it?

...You're a very suspicious man, Mr. Prosecutor.{E108:0010}
{E1D1}But why not try answering yourself for a change!?

What was an elementary school kid doing here,{E108:0008} other
than to support his father?
You had your son{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E1D1}steal your rivals' creations!

You mean like Scone?{E108:0010}
Biting bits and pieces off of them?
How would that have helped me,{E108:0008} hm?
(He's...{E108:0008} got a point...)
I'll ask you again...

Your son was the one making your entries for the
contest, wasn't he?
...My son was no confectioner.

He was an elementary school kid.{E108:0010}
{E12F:00200004}{E107:0001}{E282}I doubt he even knew how to boil an egg!
(It did seem a bit unlikely, in retrospect...)
I'll ask you again...

Your son knew the taste of your work pretty well,
I imagine, Mr. Gusto?
Hrngh!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}He was my biggest fan.{E108:0010} Of course he knew it!

In which case,{E108:0008} {E188:00300000}{E1D5}he would have been a good judge of
whether something tasted "on brand", so to speak,{E108:0008} no?
Hrngh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}Wh-What are you implying...?

You've already told us that you were suffering from a
taste disorder...
Hrrrrrrnngaahhh!

I'll admit it...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}You're good.{E108:0010} I never told anybody any of
this,{E108:0008} but you figured it all out anyway.
It's true.{E108:0010} Eighteen years ago,{E108:0008} {E188:00300000}{E1D5}I developed {E041}ageusia{E040}.
No one knew about your condition.

Indeed.{E108:0010} I doubt Mr. Frost would have wanted to
continue collaborating with you had he found out.

After all,{E108:0008} it was your job to make sure his creations
tasted good.
Therefore,{E108:0008} {E1D1}your son wasn't just here {E1D1}{E1D5}to support you!
He was helping you by taste-testing your work!
Dang.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Now it all makes sense...

Frost's stuff tasted good because it really was finished
the day before when the kid was still here!
You have a vivid imagination, Mr. Prosecutor.

But do you seriously think I'd trust a kid to tell me
how to adjust the taste of my masterpieces?
...I have some pride, you know.{E108:0010} Even back then.
Did you now...?

My designs may not have been much to write home
about back then...

...but I always knew my work tasted better than
anybody else's!

You think I'd risk everything by putting my reputation
{E1D1}in the hands of a child!?
This is just more speculation.{E108:0010} {E283}{E107:0002}That's all it is.
Arngh...!
entries.ru: Кхм...!

entries.en:
In that case,{E108:0008} I ask to speak with your son this instant!{E108:0018}
Let's see how much of your story he can corroborate!

Hngeh heh heh heh!{E108:0018}
{E12F:0020000A}Sadly for you...{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D9}{E12F:00200004}my son is no longer my concern!

As soon as I got my sense of taste back,{E108:0008} I went straight
to Zheng Fa to start my training.
...And cut off all ties with the kid for good!
WHAAAAAAT!?
You...{E108:0018} {E283}{E107:0001}You abandoned your own child?

And that ain't the half of it...{E108:0018}
{E285}No one knows where he is,{E108:0010} even now.
The cops have looked all over for him,{E108:0008} but no dice.

...So,{E108:0010} still think you can prove your asinine theory?{E108:0018}
{E12F:00200004}{E1D1}I'd like to see you try!

Hngehhh hyeh heh heh heh heh!{E108:0018} {E12F:0020000A}{E1D2}You think I care
about anything besides confectionery?{E108:0010} Think again!

I got my sense of taste back.{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}What need do I have for a son?
...Silence in the courtroom.

While Mr. Gusto's words and actions may demonstrate
a certain lack of humanity on his part...
...the Goddess of Justice...{E108:0010} {E107:0003}cannot judge him for that.

Therefore, Mr. Edgeworth,{E108:0010} I believe it is time for you
to admit defeat.

Yeah.{E108:0008} Give it up.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E280}Eighteen years is a long time for
anything to surface now --{E108:0010} proof or otherwise!
Nnrgh...!
