entries.en:
Mr. Edgeworth!{E108:0018}
We have to do something!
If we don't...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E1D1}the truth might be lost forever!
Gnrrrgh...!
(Where are you, {E1D1}Detective Gumshoe...!?)
Can't imagine whose blood it could possibly be, but...
entries.ru: Чья это кровь, ума не приложу, но...

entries.en: ...I'll get it tested right away, sir!
entries.ru: ...Сейчас же отдам на экспертизу, сэр!

entries.en: Please do, Detective.
entries.ru: Будь добр, детектив.

entries.en: (That's the last piece of the puzzle,{E108:0008} I'm sure of it.)
(Once we know whose blood it is...!)

Hey, Miles.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Sorry to cut in on your mind palace time,{E108:0008}
but I was pondering something myself...

Our friend Gusto didn't come here just to check up on
the body, did he?
You mean because he tried to open the case?

Exactamundo!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Think we have anything that might
explain why he tried to do that?

We might.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}If Detective Gumshoe can make it back in
time with a certain piece of evidence...!

That's quite enough idle chatter, defense.{E108:0010}
Now,{E108:0008} if you--
Mr. Edgeworth, sir!{E108:0020} {E188:00340000}{E1D2}Sorry to keep you waiting!
Heh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Speak of the devil.
I take it you have the test results, Detective?
Yessir!{E108:0018} {E1D1}The lab just got back to me!
Detective, please,{E108:0010} {E12F:00080004}court is in session.

Now then,{E108:0008} am I right to assume that you are bringing
us the evidence Mr. Edgeworth was just speaking of?

What!?{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Hey,{E108:0008} {E1D1}no fair!{E108:0018}
{E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1DA}{E12F:00090008}Why didn't anybody tell me about any of this!?
I, uhh...

It is indeed the evidence in question, Your Honor.{E108:0010}
It needed testing,{E108:0008} so I asked him to carry it out.

What the...?{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}Why is everybody always helping you!?
I'm supposed to be the one in charge here!
...Mr. Winner.

I'm sorry I didn't involve you,{E108:0008} but this is important.{E108:0010}
Can we at least hear what the detective has to say?

So, Detective Gumshoe,{E108:0010} what did the tests have to tell
us?
You're not going to believe this, but...!

The owner of the blood we found in the liquid at the
bottom of the Gemini case is...
...Carmelo Gusto,{E108:000C} {E280}the victim of the poison gas attack!
...What are you talking about?

Thank you, Detective.{E108:0010}
You've been very helpful.
Well...{E108:0010} {E12F:00000004}{E107:0002}it looks like my suspicions were correct.
What do you mean, Mr. Edgeworth?

Yes.{E108:0010} What DO you mean?{E108:0018}
Explain yourself.
What is the significance of this blood to this case?

It's only the very thing the perpetrator of the IS-7
Incident has been trying to hide all these years!

The fact that your blood was found inside the Gemini
case, Mr. Gusto...

...is as good as us finding your blood lying right next to
Mr. Frost's body!

Wh-Why would there be traces of your blood there, of
all places, Mr. Gusto!?
If you won't answer Her Honor, Mr. Gusto,{E108:0008} then I will.

There wasn't just blood in the liquid from the Gemini
case.{E108:0010} There were traces of salt and sugar, too.
There were...?

And if you remember,{E108:0008} one particular part of
Mr. Frost's work was allegedly very salty indeed.
Oh yeahhh...

You're talking about what Delicia told us back then,
right?{E108:0010} What was it again...?

Did they ever!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}I've never tried ices so scrumptious in
all my life!
entries.ru:
Ещё какие!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}В жизни не пробовала таких
объедений!

entries.en: Really?{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Man,{E108:0008} I wish I could've had a bite...
entries.ru: Правда?{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Эх,{E108:0008} мне бы хоть кусочек...

entries.en:
Well,{E108:0008} scrumptious except for the salty bit, of course.{E108:0010}
That was unbearable!
entries.ru:
Ну,{E108:0008} объедение, если не считать солёного места.{E108:0010}
Вот оно было невыносимо!

entries.en: The salty bit...?
entries.ru: Солёного места...?

entries.en:
It's in the other photo you've got there.{E108:0010}
This bit.{E108:0010} The...{E108:0008} harpy thing.
entries.ru:
Оно вон на том снимке, что у вас.{E108:0010}
Вот тут.{E108:0010} Эта...{E108:0008} арфовина.

entries.en: Gemini's lyre...
entries.ru: Лира Близнецов...

entries.en:
Yes.{E108:0010} The lyre --{E108:0008} and only the lyre --{E108:0008} tasted as if it had
been flavored with salt.

There were no traces of salt anywhere else in
Mr. Frost's entry.

Very interesting.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Then perhaps you can tell us,
Mr. Edgeworth...

...It's extremely distressing to watch you flounder so
horribly...

But if it's salt you're looking for,{E108:0008} I may be about to
produce some from my eyes!

(Nnrgh...!{E108:0010} Thanks,{E108:0008} but I'm already feeling their salty
cold sting as mine run down my cheeks...)

Now,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E1D1}perhaps you could present us with a slightly less
outlandish explanation?

This is...!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E284}The lamp from the IS-7 Incident...?

Indeed.{E108:0010} And I believe that the salt that gave the lyre
its flavor{E108:0008} {E285}came from just such a lamp.

Mr. von Karma had established that both salt lamps
were in Mr. Tangaroa's room at the time of the crime.
One of them was used to kill Mr. Frost.
And it was stained with his blood.

But no corresponding pool of blood was found in
Mr. Tangaroa's room.

Right.{E108:0010} Because the culprit {E285}had chucked the piece of
chocolate with that on it into the little stream.

Furthermore,{E108:0008} aside from the lyre,{E108:0008} no traces of salt
were found anywhere else in Mr. Frost's room, either.
Hey, come to think of it...

The lamps we found in Delicia's room were both
broken.
The lamps appear to be broken.
entries.ru: Лампы, похоже, разбиты.

entries.en: Bulbs are smashed...{E108:0018} Both of them...
entries.ru: Лампочки вдребезги...{E108:0018} Обе...

entries.en: Maybe they fell and broke on the floor?
entries.ru: Может, упали и разбились об пол?

entries.en:
We never did figure out how the one that wasn't used
to kill Frost got busted, but...

Are we thinking...{E108:0010} {E282}{E107:0001}maybe it had Gusto's blood on it at
some point!?
Hrrrnnngh...!

Anyone whose blood was found on one of the lamps
would have been a person of interest to the police.

So the killer needed to hide the blood somehow.{E108:0010}
And in a way that wouldn't arouse suspicion.

And you are seriously suggesting that {E188:002F0000}{E1D1}the lyre was
used to do just that...?
...I am.

I suspect that the bloody salt was somehow applied to
the lyre so that it could be hidden inside the case.

Because unlike the fountain water,{E108:0008} the sculptures
would've needed more time and care to test properly.

And so he waited and waited for his chance to dispose
of the lyre undetected.
Then...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}Then the reason he's here today is...

Eighteen years ago,{E108:0008} Mr. Frost's body and the evidence
pointing to his killer were taken away together.

This, of course,{E108:0008} was not part of the perpetrator's plan.{E108:0010}
And thus a new dilemma arose:

The possibility that the body,{E108:0008} the incriminating
evidence,{E108:0008} or both{E108:0008} would {E1D1}resurface one day.

So back he comes eighteen years later,{E108:0008} sneaking in
bright and early to try and cover his tracks.

Well, Mr. Gusto?{E108:0010}
{E107:0002}Are you finally ready to admit it?
That you are the one {E188:00200000}{E1D2}{E1D5}responsible for the IS-7 Incident!

Mr. Gusto...!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}It's all because of you that {E188:00310000}{E1D1}Samson...!

NGYEHHHH HEH HEH {E282}HEH HEH HEH HEH HEH
{E282}HEH HEH HEH HEH {E1D9}HEH HEH HEHHHHHHHH!!!
Gusto...
So I finally got caught, huh?{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}All these years later?

Nobody came close back then!{E108:0010}
Not even the big-shot prosecutor.{E108:0010} Or the attorney.

That's some impressive work, {E1D1}Mr. Prosecutor.{E108:0018}
{E107:0001}{E1D2}{E188:00310000}I have to hand it to you!
You admit it, then?{E108:0010} That you murdered Artie Frost?
But...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}he only had himself to blame...!
...What do you mean by that?

He agreed to help me.{E108:0010} We were supposed to help each
other so that one of us could win.

And whoever won was supposed to let the other use
the cookbook.

But on the day of the final,{E108:0008} {E1D9}the rat finally showed his
true colors!
Seriously, Frost!?{E108:0018} {E282}We had a deal!

Sorry.{E108:0010} I'm not helping you in the final.{E108:0018}
...Our little agreement is over, Gusto.

But...{E108:0010} But I helped YOU!{E108:0018} I spent all day yesterday
making the ice for your pieces!

...Did you?{E108:0018}
And you can prove that, I suppose?

What do you--?{E108:0010} {E107:0003}Wait...{E108:0018} {E107:0001}{E188:00310000}{E1D1}You were planning to betray
me right from the start,{E108:0008} weren't you...!?

After Frost double-crossed me,{E108:0008} {E282}I had to make my piece
for the final by myself.

And like you said,{E108:0008} my son wasn't there,{E108:0008} so I didn't
have any help with the flavor, either.

So much for the pride you claimed to have in your
ability to make delicious desserts.

Go ahead and judge.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}You have no idea what it was like
for someone like me to lose my sense of taste.

I gave up everything to become the best!{E108:0010} Everything!{E108:0018}
I take pride in that!
Something someone like you could {E1D1}never understand!

You're right.{E108:0008} {E1D1}I don't understand.{E108:0010} Do you take pride in
the fact that you resorted to murder?

Or that you abandoned your son?{E108:0018} {E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}Why would I want
to understand someone who could do such things?

...A man can't afford to rely on other people.{E108:0010}
I learned that the hard way eighteen years ago.
My son never showed up on the day of the final.

And in hindsight,{E108:0008} {E1D1}I wouldn't be surprised if Frost was
the reason why.

Why would you think that...?{E108:0018}
What exactly happened to your son?

How am I supposed to know?{E108:0010}
I told you --{E108:0010} {E1D1}he's none of my concern anymore.

And according to you guys,{E108:0008} nobody knows where he is
now either.

And you don't care...!?{E108:0018}
You're...{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}You're HORRIBLE...!

So with his disappearance,{E108:0008} so too went your chances
of winning, correct?

Yeah.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I had to find another way of getting my hands 
on that book.{E108:0010} That's when inspiration struck.

I decided to skip afternoon tea and snuck into
Tangaroa's room.

It should have been so easy.{E108:0010} {E1D1}All I had to do was
photograph the formulas I needed and get out of there.
...But then Frost showed up!
I thought I might find you here.

Stealing recipes from the famous cookbook, hm?{E108:0010}
{E107:0003}Tut tut tut.
...Frost!

What's this?{E108:0010} {E188:002F0000}{E1D1}..."A Cure for Taste Disorders"?{E108:0018}
{E107:0003}Oh, no.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}That's just too tragic!

A confectioner who can't taste anything?{E108:0010}
What will people say?
If you tell anybody,{E108:0010} I'll--!
Arngh...!
entries.ru: Кхм...!

entries.en:
You'll what...?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}You can't even hit me, you miserable worm.
...Why, you...{E1D1}!

Frost shoved me hard when I went to punch him.{E108:0010}
Knocked me clean off my feet.

I crashed into one of the lamps.{E108:0010}
Must have been when my blood got on it.
So Mr. Frost wasn't the first to get hurt...

When it was all over,{E108:0008} I realized I had to get rid of that
blood somehow,{E108:0008} so I scraped off all the bloodied bits.

I dissolved those salt shavings in some flavored ice
mixture,{E108:0008} {E1D5}and brushed it all over the harp!

And that's how you made the evidence linking you to
the murder vanish...!
...Frost was going to blackmail me.

He would have made me give him money to keep quiet
about my condition.
So you decided you had to kill him!?

Why would I let him live?{E108:0010} {E107:0001}Would you want someone
holding something like that over your head?

Besides,{E108:0008} he's the one who drew first blood.{E108:0010}
Makes for a solid case of self-defense, don't you think?
(So that was the impetus behind it all...)
Anyway,{E108:0008} I initially took the lamp to Frost's room.

Went straight there once I'd figured out how I was
going to hide the bloody part.

...Inspired by all the {E285}ice-sculpting tools lying about the
place, I guess?

You're not as dumb as you pretend to be.{E108:0018} Yeah,{E108:0008}
{E1D1}figured I could use them to chip it off and grind it up.

Once that was done,{E108:0008} {E188:00340000}{E1D1}{E107:0001}painting the stuff all over the
harp was easy.

But...{E108:0010} why Samson?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}Why did you have to frame him...!?
I never meant for the cops to pin it on him.
That was your fault.{E108:0010} {E283}{E107:0001}You and the rest of them.

Why do you think {E188:002F0000}{E1D1}I went to the trouble of placing the
lamps and cloths back in Scone's room?

...There's only one reason to plant the murder weapon
in the room of another contestant.
And that's to cast suspicion on that person.

WHAAAAAAT!?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}Y-You tried to frame me, Gustypants!?

I respected Tangaroa.{E108:0010} He was the best.{E108:0010}
A true champion.
I would never have wanted him to take the fall.

But you --{E108:0008} {E1D5}{E1D1}you're a fraud.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Your work wasn't even real.{E108:0010}
You had no respect for our craft at all.
You deserved to be punished for what you did!
Oh, Gusty...!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E280}H-How could you!?

And had you refrained from eating Tangaroa's work,{E108:0008}
{E107:0001}{E1D5}Frost's body wouldn't have been found.

My plan was to wait until Tangaroa was judging your
room.

That's when I'd sneak the corpse into Frost's room and
freeze it.

But thanks to you,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E1D5}Bound here found it before I had a
chance to retreive it...!

I don't understand...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}Why did you need to freeze his
body at all?
Ha!{E108:0010} Why indeed...?
Mr. Edgeworth...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}surely you must know!?
Why did Mr. Gusto need to freeze Mr. Frost's body?

Mr. Gusto needed to freeze it in order to pass it off as
an ice sculpture.

Now look what you've done, Mr. Edgeworth!{E108:0010}
Ms. Bound's so lost in her thoughts,{E108:0008} {E1D1}she's frozen up!

S-Sorry about that.{E108:0010}
(I guess that wasn't it...)
Please, Mr. Edgeworth!{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}Tell us the truth this time!
The reason Mr. Gusto had to freeze the body...

...was to hide the true scene of the crime from the
police.

Umm...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}So he wanted to...{E108:0010} confuse them over where it
really happened...?

That's one heck of an icy glare from Judge Gavèlle,
Mr. Edgeworth!
(Gnrk...{E108:0010} Alright,{E108:0008} message received...)

...Mr. Gusto needed to freeze Mr. Frost's body in order
to obscure the time of death.

If they'd determined that the murder occurred during
afternoon tea,{E108:0008} he would have been an obvious suspect.

Hngeh heh {E1D2}heh heh!{E108:0018}{E12F:0020000A}
{E107:0002}Bingo!

Freezing Frost's body wasn't simple.{E108:0010}
Preparing everything took time.

So I decided to put his body in the chest in Tangaroa's
room while I got everything ready in Frost's.
At the time,{E108:0008} it seemed like the perfect hiding place.

Never counted on some gluttonous pharmacist
showing up{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E188:00310000}{E1D1}{E1D5}{E173:0000}and making the whole ship collapse!

I still don't get it, though.{E108:0010}
{E1D1}Why disguise the body as an ice sculpture at all?

The sooner it was found,{E108:0008} the smaller the effect of
freezing it would've had on masking the time of death.

Therefore,{E108:0008} he needed to disguise it,{E108:0008} at least until it'd
fully frozen.
How awful...!

Using Mr. Frost's own work to help you cover up the
truth behind his murder!

Ironically,{E108:0008} Tangaroa would have been just fine if the
body hadn't been found before I got it out of his room.

If only things had gone to plan.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}{E283}{E12F:00200004}He wouldn't even have
been arrested,{E108:0008} let alone convicted.

You...{E108:0010} You mean...{E108:0010} {E1D1}It was my fault...?{E108:0010}{E175:002400030000}{E108:0008}
{E1D1}Everything that happened to Samson...
It was all because{E108:0008} {E1D1}I found the body...!?

Don't let him get inside your head, Judes.{E108:0010}
None of this is your fault.

If it wasn't Samson,{E108:0008} it would have been Delicia instead.{E108:0010}
She would've been the one they arrested.

Either way,{E108:0008} there's only one person to blame here,{E108:0010} and
that's Gusto.

...It didn't help that the initial detective was so bad at
his job, either.

He never even told the prosecutor that the body had
vanished!

So then,{E108:0008} {E188:002F0000}{E1D1}Mr. von Karma had unwittingly placed
Mr. Tangaroa under arrest in the absence of a body...?

I mean...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I guess it would explain why he was so keen
to wrap things up.

Still,{E108:0008} {E188:002F0000}{E1D5}you'd think he'd notice something as big as that if
he'd taken a look at a few reports, right?

(Not if someone had been {E1D5}deliberately distorting the
facts of the case, though...)

Either way,{E108:0008} it seems that Mr. von Karma didn't know
about the body until {E1D1}after the arrest had been made.

But admitting that would have spoiled his perfect
record.

So he kept it to himself,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E283}and proceeded to prosecute
Mr. Tangaroa regardless!
C-Can this really be true...!?

You don't feel bad at all?{E108:0018} {E12F:00020001}{E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}Somebody spent eighteen
years in prison because of you!

Hngeh heh heh...!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}Sticks and stones, girlie.{E108:0008} Sticks and stones.

What a jerk!{E108:0018}
{E1D1}I oughta arrest you right now, pal!
...I'm afraid I can't allow you to do that, Detective.
The judge is right.{E108:0018} {E12F:00200004}{E283}You can't lay a finger on me!
What!?{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E280}Why!?{E108:0018} {E1D1}You just confessed to murder!
HNGEH {E1D1}HEH {E1D1}HEHHHH!
No idea, huh?{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E1D1}Then I guess I'd better lay it out for you!
-- Why You Can't Arrest Me --
I killed Frost eighteen years ago.

The statute of limitations for murder in this country is
fifteen years.
You do the math!{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}You can't arrest me!
You think I'd have confessed otherwise!?

That's right...!{E108:0010}
{E188:00310000}{E1D1}{E1D5}The statute of limitations is only fifteen years!
Is this...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}really the end of the line, Mr. Edgeworth?

...{E1D1}Nngh...!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Once the statute has expired,{E108:0008} {E188:00340000}{E1D1}he can't be
charged, so...
...How unfortunate, Mr. Edgeworth.

I'm afraid that both Mr. Gusto's confession and your
deductions...{E108:0010} {E284}will have to be struck from the record.

And that Mr. Tangaroa's conviction will remain in
place.

But...!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}We've finally proven that the police never had
Mr. Frost's body in their possession!

Even if we can't arrest Mr. Gusto,{E108:0010} {E188:00340000}{E1DA}surely Mr. Tangaroa
has grounds for a retrial on that basis?
Does he?{E108:0010} I wouldn't be so sure.

I'm afraid that the Goddess's judgments are {E1D1}somewhat
harder to overturn than you might imagine.

(So the Committee means for the verdict from
eighteen years ago to stand no matter what...!?)

HNGEHHH HEH {E1D2}HEH HEHHH!{E108:0018}
Bad luck, Mr. Prosecutor!

(There must be something we can do!{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}Something to bring Mr. Gusto down!)
-- Why You Can't Arrest Me --
I killed Frost eighteen years ago.

The statute of limitations for murder in this country is
fifteen years.
You do the math! You can't arrest me!
You think I'd have confessed otherwise!?

I later went to Zheng Fa to train, and I finally became
the best in the world.

As for Tangaroa, I didn't stick around for his final
court appearance.

Mr. Gusto is no ordinary opponent.{E108:0010} {E1D1}He's gone eighteen
years without his crimes being exposed.

Think, Mr. Edgeworth!{E108:0018}
{E188:00310000}{E1D1}There must be some way for us to arrest him!

The guy's probably watched a few legal dramas before,{E108:0008}
{E1D5}but he's no lawyer.{E108:0010} {E12F:000A0001}Not like you and me.

...There's gotta be some loophole {E1D1}somewhere we can
use.{E108:0010} There's just gotta.

(He's right...{E108:0010} Mr. Gusto is just an armchair attorney,
after all...)

The passage of time {E108:0010}{E12F:00000004}{E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1DA}doesn't diminish what you did,
Mr. Gusto!
It sure diminishes one thing, though.
Your ability to arrest me!

Oh,{E108:0008} we can arrest you!{E108:0010} We can arrest you real good!{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}I could have you in cuffs before you even blink, pal!
Right, Mr. Edgeworth!?

Um...{E108:0008} I...{E108:0018}{E12F:00000001} This issue isn't as open and shut as you're
making it out to be, Detective.

Hngeh {E108:0004}heh {E108:0004}{E1D2}heh {E108:0004}heh!{E108:0018}
{E107:0001}{E12F:0020000A}You can't touch me!{E108:0010} It's too late for that!

Depending on your actions over the last eighteen
years, {E108:0010}{E107:0001}{E1D5}{E1D1}{E12F:00000009}the statute may not have expired yet!

Hngeh heh heh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}This ought to be good.{E108:0010}
Alright,{E108:0008} I got nothing to hide.
If there's something you want to ask,{E108:0008} ask it.

...Very well.{E108:0010} Tell us where you've been and what
you've been doing since the incident.
Sure.

Not long after the contest,{E108:0008} {E1D1}I was able to cure my taste
disorder thanks to the formula from that book.

And not so long after that,{E108:0008} I went to Zheng Fa to really
buckle down and hone my craft.

That explains a lot.{E108:0010} We tried to contact you after the
fact,{E108:0008} but I guess you were {E188:00300000}{E1D5}long gone by then, huh.

...around a year after the murder.{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E12F:00200000}It was before Tangaroa's last day in court.

Going to Zheng Fa was the best thing I ever did.{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E12F:00200007}Flavor,{E108:0008} design --{E108:0010} {E1D2}{E1D5}I'm the full package now!

And all on the backs of those whose lives you
destroyed.
HNGEHHH HEH HEH {E1D2}HEH HEH HEHHH!

What's an omelet without a few eggs,{E108:0008} hm?{E108:0018}
Nothing, Mr. Prosecutor!{E108:0010} Nothing!
You're EVIL...
Sticks and stones, girlie!
You can't arrest me,{E108:0010} {E1D2}{E107:0001}and that's all that matters!

(Arngh...!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I need more to work with.{E108:0010}
{E1D5}There has to be something I can get out of him...)

(Maybe I can push him further on the statements he
just made.{E108:0010} {E188:002F0000}{E1D1}Is there anything I should follow up on...?)

I'd like you to tell us more about your training in
Zheng Fa, if you wouldn't mind.
Fine.

Would you mind telling us more about Mr. Tangaroa's
final day in court?
Fine.

(...No,{E108:0008} there wasn't anything in particular.{E108:0010}
I just need to think things over a little more.)
Never say never, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D5}{E1D1}Nothing is impossible!
Really?{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Come on,{E108:0008} give it up.

Your father couldn't catch me.{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E283}{E12F:00200004}What makes you think you can?
Arngh...!
entries.ru: Кхм...!

entries.en:
(He would've solved the whole case if it hadn't been
for Mr. von Karma obstructing him at every turn.)

(And now,{E108:0008} {E1D1}the statue of limitations is threatening to
inter the truth of this case forever...!)

Don't listen to him, Mr. Edgeworth!{E108:0018} {E188:00310000}{E1D1}You can't give up!{E108:0010}
Not now!

We're doing this for your dad...{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}so we have to see it
through to the end!
Kay...
entries.ru: Кей...

entries.en:
The truth is right there for the taking!{E108:0008}{E152:0002000A0008}{E112:0002} {E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D2}What kind of
Great Thieves are we if we don't grab it for ourselves!?

I'm...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}not a Great Thief, Kay...{E108:0010}
But you're right.

Carmelo Gusto...{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E188:00200000}{E1D2}{E1D5}I won't allow you to make off with the truth!

HNGEH HEH {E1D2}HEH HEHHH!{E108:0018}
{E107:0003}Do your worst!

That was the only reason?{E108:0010} Because you knew the
statute had expired?

Ngeh heh heh!{E108:0018} {E1D1}Why else would I do it?{E108:0018}
{E1D1}Why would anybody?
Not that I'd planned on it ever coming out, of course.
...And why was that?
Because I'm finally the world's greatest confectioner!

And petty stuff like this {E283}only gets in the way of me and
my craft.

So you're more concerned about you and your rep
than the fact that Samson's still rotting in jail?

I've seen some pieces of work in my time,{E108:0010} but you...{E108:0010}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}{E1D5}You're just flat-out unforgivable...!

Who cares about forgiveness?{E108:0018} I did what I did.{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E12F:00200004}{E188:00340000}{E1DA}I don't need you to understand any of it!

Alright Miles,{E108:0008} it's official.{E108:001E} {E1D5}{E17A:000400000001}{E12F:000A0002}{E107:0003}{E1D1}Uncle Eddie is mad.{E108:0010}
And that doesn't happen often.
...You're not the only one.

But don't worry.{E108:0010} {E1D5}He won't get away with this.{E108:0010}
Not if I can help it!

Zheng Fa?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E188:002F0000}{E1D1}And you were there for a while, I imagine?

Yeah.{E108:0010} I left some time after the investigation had
wrapped up.

I'd been meaning to go there and start my studies for
a while.
And thanks to the hard work I put in...
...my designs are now world class!
Whoooooa!{E108:0018} That's amaaazing!
...You like it?{E108:0010} It's yours.
Really!?{E108:0018} Alright!
(So he spent some time in Zheng Fa training...)

And you weren't summoned as a witness at any point
by the prosecution or the defense?

I had more important things to do than worry about
some court case.
I was busy getting ready to go and become the best.

Gregory and me searched high and low for the guy.{E108:0010}
Seemed like he didn't want to be found.

(Sounds like he played his cards right and managed to
avoid setting foot in court.)
You're lying, Mr. Gusto.{E108:0010} And this proves it!

...This is no time for meditation!{E108:0010}
{E1D2}{E188:00310000}I need you to look at the evidence!

Well, I don't need to look at it.{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}It's garbage.{E108:0018} And you need to try harder.
Nnrgh...!
entries.ru: Нгрх...!

entries.en:
If you're looking to improve your professional skills,{E108:0008}
I wholeheartedly recommend going to Zheng Fa.
This evidence will expose the truth at last!
...Pathetic.{E108:0018} Is this your idea of a joke?

(It's not...{E108:0010} but this evidence doesn't point to any kind
of contradiction at all, does it...!?)
May I continue?
There's a contradiction in your testimony, Mr. Gusto.

...Oh?{E108:0010}
You do like to spout some real nonsense, don't you?

You're no match for your father.{E108:0010}
{E107:0003}Not by a long shot.
How dare y--!

Hngeh heh heh heh!{E108:0010}
Too close to home?{E108:0010} My bad.

The statute of limitations for murder is subject to the
following condition:

"{E041}The statute is {E1D5}suspended should the suspect flee to a
foreign country.{E040}"

Which means that the time you spent abroad{E108:0008} {E107:0001}{E283}doesn't
count toward the total time under the statute!

No way!{E108:0018} {E107:0001}{E1D1}So it's like someone hit pause while he was in
Zheng Fa!?
It appears that there may be time left on the clock yet.

But that will depend on how long you stayed in Zheng
Fa, Mr. Gusto...

Three years{E040}!{E108:0020} {E12F:000A0002}{E107:0003}Hold on...!{E108:001E}{E12F:000A0005}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}Nobody say anything until I've done the math...

The murder happened eighteen years back...{E108:0018}
{E12F:000A0002}The statute is {E1D1}fifteen years...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D5}add the three overseas...

Mr. Edgeworth,{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E188:00340000}{E1D1}you did it!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}The statute hasn't expired after all!

(Gnrgh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D5}He's just been stringing us along this whole
time...!)

Wh-Why is he laughing!?{E108:0018} {E107:0002}We're good, aren't we?{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}We can arrest him now!
I hate to break it to you, little sis, but...

...IS-7 went down {E1D5}{E12F:00020001}at the end of December.{E108:0010}
It's April now,{E108:0008} which means...

...strictly speaking,{E108:0008} {E188:002F0000}{E1D5}{E17A:000400000000}it's been eighteen years and four
months since Frost's murder.

If Gusto's stay in Zheng Fa really lasted three years on
the nose,{E108:0008} it's not enough.{E108:0010} {E107:0003}{E1D1}We're a few months short.
What did I tell you?{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E283}You can't touch me!
HNGEHHH HEH {E1D1}HEH HEHHH!

(I hate to admit it,{E108:0008} {E1D1}but he'd read the board well when
he made his confession...)
How unfortunate, Mr. Edgeworth.

If only the statute had been suspended for another
year...
Nngh...!
entries.ru: Нгх...!

entries.en:
Those who would overturn the Goddess's judgment{E108:0010}
{E107:0003}{E1D5}{E1D1}must be willing to pay the price should they fail.
And you, Mr. Edgeworth...{E108:0010} have failed.
Nngh...{E108:0010} {E107:0003}{E283}NNGHOOO{E1D2}{E1D5}OOOOO{E107:0002}OOOOO{E1D5}{E1D2}OOOOO{E1D1}OOOGH!
(There must be...{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}something I can do...!)

I knew it...{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E188:00310000}{E1D5}Well, if the law can't bring Mr. Gusto to justice,{E108:0008} then...
Judes...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}What are you thinking...?

There's no need to go adding to your rap sheet just
yet.

We're not done here.{E108:0010} Far from it.{E108:0010}
{E107:0003}{E188:00300000}{E1D5}'Cause there's still a way we can nail him.
There is...?

Alright, Milesarino.{E108:0008} {E1D1}Pep talk.{E108:0010} I need you to think back
over everything we know about the case.

Gusto's overlooked one critical thing that you yourself
were led to believe wrongly about.
Which is...?
He wasn't there for Samson's last trial,{E108:0008} remember?

Best I can tell,{E108:0008} {E12F:000A0002}{E188:00300000}{E1D5}{E12F:00000009}he doesn't seem to know what the final
verdict that came down that day is.
...Which means there's still one way left to us.

Crack open your{E108:0008} {E12F:000A0003}{E1D5}"{E041}Statutes for Dummies{E040}" there and
take another look.

Seventeen years ago,{E108:0008} they really did a number on
Samson and framed him like a pretty picture.

But if we make good use of that verdict now,{E108:0010} {E188:00200000}{E1D2}{E1D5}{E12F:000A0002}we can
make Gusto pay in full for what he's done.

"{E041}Those who would overturn the Goddess's judgment{E108:0010}
{E1D5}must be willing to pay the price should they fail{E040}"...

Samson's my client, Miles.{E108:0010} {E1D1}And I can't bring myself to
use the source of his pain as a weapon in this fight.

So whether we play our last card or not...{E108:0010} {E107:0003}{E1D1}it's gonna
have to be up to you.

(Bringing Mr. Gusto to justice can only happen if I use
the outcome of that hard-fought trial.)

(So...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}should I raise an objection and play that card or
not?)

(If I don't do something now,{E108:0008} {E107:0001}Mr. Gusto will never see
his day in court.)

(And Mr. Tangaroa will never get another chance to
clear his name.)
(Is this really what I believe --{E108:0010} what I'm fighting for?)

(My father and Mr. von Karma...{E108:0010}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}One sought to reveal the truth,{E108:0008} {E1D1}the other to hide it...)

(I know which path I choose to follow...{E108:0018}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}{E188:00200000}{E1D5}{E12F:00000009}The one that seeks to reveal the {E041}truth{E042}!)
This court has reached its final verdict.

The record will state that Mr. Gusto has been found
{E188:002F0000}{E1D5}{E041}not guilty{E040} on all counts.

No, Your Honor!{E108:0018}
{E283}Mr. Carmelo Gusto is absolutely {E041}guilty{E040}!

And I refuse to let him walk away!{E108:0010}{E172:000C0000}
{E107:0001}{E1D1}His crimes are too unspeakable {E1D5}to go unpunished!

...Do you mean to suggest{E108:0008} {E1D5}that you have grounds upon
which to call for his arrest?
...I do.

(Now to show Judge Gavèlle something that proves the
statute of limitations hasn't yet expired...!){E106}{E163:00010000}{E100:0001}{E164:00830008}{E100:0000}{E12F:00000009}{E101:00000000}{E107:0001}{E1D1}{E188:00340000}Consider this piece of evidence, if you will!

...The court rules the evidence inadmissible.{E108:0010}{E112:0008} {E12F:0008000E}{E112:0008}{E12F:0008000F}On the
grounds that it appears to be entirely irrelevant.
Nnrgh!

Believe me, Mr. Edgeworth,{E108:0008} I understand your
frustration.
It isn't easy giving up on a lost cause.
(I will not give up!{E108:0018} I will see that justice is done!)
(Mr. Tangaroa's trial lasted a year.)

(And though it ended with a verdict that {E1D1}couldn't have
been more wrong...)

(...that very verdict may be what {E1D1}finally sees Mr. Gusto
arrested!)

Very well.{E108:0010} Is there a particular page of the IS-7 case
file you would like us to refer to?
Take a look at the case overview, Your Honor.

I am sure we are all very familiar with the particulars
of this case by now, Mr. Edgeworth.

And I fail to see how they have any relevance to the
statute of limitations.
(Arngh...!{E108:0010} {E107:0001}Now's not the time for slip-ups!)

(I need to use a certain so-called {E1D1}{E041}fact{E042} to finally reveal
the {E1D1}{E041}truth{E042}!{E108:0010} Only that wrong can set things right!)

Take a look at the page concerning the victim, Your
Honor.

Why?{E108:0010} {E107:0002}What more could we possibly hope to learn
about Mr. Frost that would be of any relevance?

...Perhaps it would be better{E108:0008} {E12F:00080007}{E107:0001}{E188:00310000}{E1D1}to simply admit defeat,
Mr. Edgeworth?
(I'm so close...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}I can't mess this up now!)

(Stay calm and think, Miles!{E108:0010} {E285}This next move might {E1D1}put
the whole case to rest at last!)

I'd like to direct your attention to the page concerning
the suspect.

As you can see...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Samson Tangaroa was convicted as
{E1D5}an {E041}accomplice{E040}.

And it took around {E1D5}{E041}one year{E040} from his indictment for
that verdict to be reached.
Yes...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}That does seem to be the case...

The book you gave us details certain {E1D1}conditions
pertaining to the statute of limitations for murder:

One of them, as I mentioned,{E108:0008} is that the {E041}statute is
suspended if the suspect flees the country{E040}.
And another...

...states that{E108:0008} {E188:00200000}{E1D1}{E1D5}{E173:0000}"{E041}the statute is suspended from the time of
any accomplice's indictment to the end of their trial.{E040}"

Yup.{E108:0018} Guess you were in Zheng Fa when the verdict
came down.

Samson was convicted as an accomplice,{E108:0008} not as the
main perpetrator.

...Which is clearly news to you.{E108:0010}
And not good news either, amirite?

T-Tangaroa wasn't an accomplice to anyone!{E108:001E} {E1D1}{E188:00340000}He was
innocent, and you know it!{E108:0010} He--

Oh, we know it.{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E12F:00000004}It's what we've been trying to prove
all along.

And in a pleasing twist of fate,{E108:0008} his wrongful conviction{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E283}{E12F:00000009}will be the very thing that sets him free!
If you spent {E041}three years{E040} in Zheng Fa...

And your "{E041}accomplice{E040}" Samson Tangaroa was on trial
for {E041}one year{E040}...

It means you can still be charged with Mr. Frost's
murder up to {E1D5}{E041}nineteen years{E040} after the fact.
In other words...
...the statute of limitations{E108:0010} {E1D1}hasn't expired at all!
HNNNNGGGGAAA{E1D1}{E1D5}RRRRGGGHHH!
The Goddess's judgment is {E1D5}infallible.

But that of her servants, it appears, is not.{E108:0010} It seems
the prosecutor in charge of this case {E1D1}may have erred.

Unbelievably,{E108:0008} {E188:00310000}{E1D1}we may have no choice but to instigate a
full inquiry...

N-No...!{E108:0018} {E188:00310000}{E1D2}How could this...!?{E108:001E} {E107:0002}You weren't supposed
to be able to--!{E1EA:00010026}{E104}{E100:0001}{E123:000A000000040000}{E124:0000}{E100:0000}{E101:000A000B}{E107:0003}Eighteen years...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}That's a long time to let somebody
else suffer for your crimes.

It's time to pay the piper, Gusto.{E108:0010}
And not a moment too soon.
HRRRRRRAAARRRGH!

But...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I'm finally the greatest...!{E108:0010}
{E1D1}My brilliance has been recognized...!

I gave up {E1D1}everything for this...!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E188:00310000}{E1D1}Everything!{E108:0010}
{E107:0001}{E1D5}{E1D1}Even my son!
...More's the pity.

But you can't run from the law forever!
{E152:0000000C000D}{E108:001E}{E107:0001}{E283}{E173:0000}Because the bill's come due at last!

Hngh{E107:0007}........................
.................................{E108:0082}{E104}{E100:0001}{E12F:00200004}{E108:003C}{E100:0000}{E188:00A70000}{E12F:0020000C}{E133:0020000D00C00060000000000000}{E101:00200020}{E107:0003}{E1D1}HNGH...{E108:0018} {E107:0003}{E1DA}HNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNGGGGGGHHH!!!{E108:0010}{E112:0020}{E104}{E12F:0020000E}{E137:0020000F}{E101:00200020}{E107:0002}{E281}HNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN{E280}NNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
NNNNNNNNNNNNNN{E282}NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN{E104}{E101:00200020}{E107:0001}{E280}NNNNGAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
AAAAAAAAAAAAAA{E281}AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA{E104}{E101:00200020}{E107:0001}AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA{E1D2}AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
AAAAAAAAAAAARR{E1D5}RRRRRGGGGGGHHHHHH!!!
Mr. Gusto's all set for his trip downtown, sir!
I...{E108:0010} I suppose so...
Judes...

I'm so sorry, everybody...{E108:0010}
I've caused you all so much trouble...

But...{E108:0010} thank you.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Thank you so much for bringing
Mr. Gusto to justice at last.

...I'm afraid there's no escaping the consequences of
your actions, Ms. Bound.

But those actions were born of the legal mistakes that
were made all those years ago.{E108:0010} We all know that.

...So allow me to apologize in return.{E108:0010}
On behalf of the prosecution.

Oh, no...{E108:0010} I have no one to blame but myself for it all,{E108:0010}
starting with those sculptures...

Hey, Judes...{E108:0010} You think maybe you might want me to
represent you?
I'm not some nervous newbie anymore.

And there's no way I'm letting you take the rap for
everything.
Oh...!{E108:0020} {E107:0003}I'd be honored.{E108:0010} Thank you, Mr. Fender.
Uh, sorry, ma'am...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}but you gotta come with me now...
...Of course.
entries.ru: ...Разумеется.

entries.en: ...Judge Gavèlle.
Why did you lie to us?

..."Lie"?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}What are you talking about?

You implied that there was {E041}no case for a retrial{E040}.{E108:0010}
But as we've proven,{E108:0008} that wasn't true.

Surely anyone truly committed to seeing justice done 
would have called one as soon as the body was found?

............{E108:0018}
{E107:0003}I am under no obligation to answer such questions.

(And you clearly have no intention of doing so,
either...)

Truly,{E108:0008} you are proving to be quite a threat to the
Committee for Prosecutorial Excellence.

As such,{E108:0008} you give me little choice but to report back
on your continued transgressions.

No doubt you will be called to appear before the
Committee in due course.
Now...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E285}I must be on my way.

What the heck!?{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}{E1D1}And after you caught the real killer and everything...!
Isn't that what prosecutors are supposed to do!?

...Regardless of how it may all play out,{E108:0008} I will never
regret what we accomplished here today.
Mr. Edgeworth...
Yes?
entries.ru: Да?

entries.en:
Why did you stick your nose in this case anyway?{E108:0010}
{E1D1}You weren't even on the job.
My job is to bring the truth to light, Mr. Winner.
Not only as a prosecutor,{E108:0008} but as a person.

I wouldn't expect you to understand.{E108:0010} Not as long as
you believe that closing a case makes you a winner.
What was that all about?
Eustace still has a lot to learn is all.
Milesy-Wilesey!
Y-Yes...?

I just wanted to say old Greggy Pegleg would have
been {E1D1}proud of you today!{E108:0010} Oh, look at me tearing up!
That,{E108:0008} and...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}thanks for helping poor Sammypoople.
O-{E108:0008}Of course...

Hey, Edgey!{E108:0018}
{E107:0002}Looks like you cleared everything up, huh?

So...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}what happened, exactly?{E108:0010}
I was kinda busy sketching.
...Wait.{E108:0010} Where did Judy and Verity go?
Wow...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}{E1D1}You really weren't paying attention, were you?

(Though I am loath to admit it...{E108:0008} Larry's sketches did
come through for us on more than one occasion.)
(Not that I'm about to tell him that...)

Quit it with the glaring, will ya!?{E108:0018}
Whatever I did,{E108:0010} I'm sorryyyyy!
Calm down, Larry.{E108:0010} I wasn't glaring at you.

Heh heh!{E108:0010} {E107:0002}You totally were!{E108:0018}
You're just like your pop.{E108:0010} He was a terrible liar, too.
Listen,{E108:0008} I'm gonna head out.
Need to fill Samson in on what went down today.
You wanna come with?
...Yes,{E108:0008} of course.
Great!{E108:0018} Then I'm coming, too!

April 2, 4:56 PM
{E20D}Detention Center - Visitor's Room

...So what's Mr. Tangaroa like?{E108:0010} I can't wait to finally
meet him.
Oh,{E108:0008} he's a real sweetheart.{E108:0010} You'll love him.

Even while locked up,{E108:0008} he can't help but make all sorts
of cookies and cakes for everyone.

It's why {E285}3 PM Cakestravaganza is a thing for prisoners
and guards alike.

Really?{E108:0010} {E107:0002}That sounds awesome!{E108:0010}
{E1D1}You think there'll be any left for us to try?

(Hmm...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Didn't we find {E1CB:005300020000}a few slices of chocolate cake in
the prison the other day...?)

(Could they have been some of Mr. Tangaroa's baked
goods...?)
...Gummy!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}{E188:002F0000}{E1D1}What are you doing here?

I heard you all were coming to see Mr. Tangaroa,{E108:0010} {E1D1}so
I volunteered to escort him.

Hello, new friends.{E108:0018}
I'm Samson Tangaroa.
Prosecutor Miles Edgeworth,{E108:0008} at your service.
And I'm Mr. Edgeworth's trusty sidekick,{E108:0010} {E188:00340000}{E1D1}{E12F:00020008}{E1D1}Kay Faraday!
Heh heh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}It's very nice to meet you both.
Miles here is Gregory's son.

...Your father was very kind to me,{E108:0008} and fought so hard
for my case.

But in the end...{E108:0010} {E1D1}I betrayed him.{E108:0010}
I made a false confession and...

...Don't worry, Mr. Tangaroa.{E108:0010}
Mr. Fender has explained everything to me.

Sure did.{E108:0010} And now we're here to tell you the truth
about what happened eighteen years ago.
Judy did all that...{E108:0010} {E1D1}for me...?

Crazy kid racked her brain for eighteen years until
she'd finally figured out how to set you free.

What can I say?{E108:0010} Turns out,{E108:0008} she really would do
anything for you.

Oh, Judy...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I never did anything to deserve such
devotion...

Come now, Mr. Tangaroa...{E108:0010} I think we all know that's
not true.

The bond between the two of you has held strong for
all these years, after all.
(I guess I'd better show him.)

(Which piece of evidence is proof of the bond
Mr. Tangaroa and Ms. Bound share...?){E106}{E163:00010000}{E100:0001}{E164:007C0004}{E100:0000}{E12F:001A0001}{E101:001A001D}{E107:0002}...This...{E108:0010} shows the bond between Judy and I?

I...{E108:0008} guess I can see it...{E108:0010}
These things can take all kinds of shapes, after all...

I,{E108:0008} erm...{E108:0010}
(That wasn't what I meant at all...!)
...Thank you.
entries.ru: ...Спасибо.

entries.en: Those chocolates...{E108:0010} {E107:0003}{E285}Judy made them,{E108:0010} didn't she?
...Yes,{E108:0008} she did.
They're super delicious and sweet!

Ms. Bound continued making them just as you taught
her,{E108:0008} even after that fateful day.

So that there would always be some waiting for you...{E108:0010}
when you finally came home.
Judy...

Heh heh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}I bet they're {E1D1}beyond super sweet, then,{E108:0008}
aren't they?

Very much so, I'm afraid.{E108:0028}
{E12F:00000001}I only wish we could hand them to you...
Don't worry, sir!{E108:0010} {E188:00340000}{E1D2}I'll make sure he gets them later!

(Which would be a clear breach of prison policy...{E108:0010} Not
that I have the authority now to stop him anyway.)
Heh heh...{E108:0010} {E107:0002}Thank you very much.

You know, Detective,{E108:0010} something about you reminds
me of Detective Badd.

Really, pal!?{E108:0018}
{E12F:00010007}'Cause I look up to him a lot.{E108:0010} {E1D1}He's my role model!

You don't say?{E108:0018} It seems Fate likes to bring people of
all sorts together, huh?
...You hang in there, Samson.{E108:0010} Just a little longer.
I should be able to get you out soon.

I'm sorry it's taken so long.{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Nobody should have to
wait eighteen years to get justice.

Don't be silly, Eddie.{E108:0018} {E107:0002}I'm the one who should be saying
sorry.
Or rather...
Samson...
entries.ru: Самсон...

entries.en:
Well,{E108:0008} I guess it's my turn to wait for Judy to come
home now.

I'd better make sure there's something delicious on the
table for her when she finally walks through that door.
Don't let me down, Eddie.
...Leave it to me, big guy!

(The IS-7 Incident...{E108:0018} {E107:0002}It's been eighteen long years,{E108:0008} but
this case we'd inherited from my father...)
(...is finally coming to a close.)
Hey, Miles.{E108:0010} {E107:0003}Thanks for today.

And sorry for forcing you to make the final call like
that.
Not at all.{E108:0010} I simply made the call that felt right to me.
Huh?{E108:0018} {E107:0002}What are you guys talking about?

You know how Samson was {E1D1}{E041}wrongfully convicted{E040}?{E108:0010} We
had to pretend that he wasn't in order to nail Gusto.

But to use his false conviction against him,{E108:0008} even to
save him...
As his lawyer,{E108:0008} {E1D1}I just couldn't bring myself to do it.
Yeah,{E108:0008} I can see that...

But now that Gusto's behind bars,{E108:0008} I can finally start to
get that wrongful conviction overturned.
Yes.{E108:0010} {E107:0002}And I am sure you will.

Wait a minute...!{E108:0018} {E107:0002}Does this mean that even if you were
only doing what's right...

If the false conviction had been overturned before
today,{E108:0008} {E1D1}Mr. Gusto would've gotten away scot-free?

Yup...{E108:0008}{E112:000A} {E107:0002}{E12F:000A0009}It's what we folks in the trade like to call{E108:0008} {E188:002F0000}{E1D1}a {E041}legal
contradiction{E040}.
The law is far from perfect.
Because of things like "legal contradictions", right...?

Yeah,{E108:0010} but you never know.{E108:0010} Things might change.{E108:0018}
The law's always evolving,{E108:0008} just like us humans.
Your Uncle Eddie and Milesarino included,{E108:0010} {E107:0001}{E1D1}{E12F:000A0001}amirite?

(The potential for growth and change...{E108:0010} in people and
the law, huh...)

Are you going to keep fighting crime as a prosecutor,{E108:0020}
{E1D1}or help people as an attorney?

Something tells me you've got a big decision ahead of
you.{E108:0010} One only you can answer.
...I know.

Well,{E108:0018} {E107:0002}let's just say {E1D1}I won't complain {E172:001E0001}if you show up at
the office one day.
And on that note,{E108:0008} {E1D1}it's time for me to skedaddle.

I owe you big time,{E108:0008} and I always repay my debts,{E108:0010} but
for now...

Did he seem kind of in a hurry to get out of here to
you?
...He did.

(And honestly speaking,{E108:0008} I'm the one who owes him a
debt of gratitude.)

(After all,{E108:0008} he gave me the chance to {E1D1}reckon with my
father's final case.)

When I was a boy,{E108:0008} all I ever dreamed of was becoming
an attorney like my father.

But then,{E108:0008} during my time with Mr. von Karma,{E108:0008}
{E1D5}I learned the way of the prosecutor instead.

Eventually,{E108:0008} with the help of some good friends,{E108:0008} I found
my own voice and a new way to live.
But now...

...now my career as a prosecutor is at risk of being
taken away from me.

It may be time to take another long,{E108:0008} hard look at how
I want to live my life.{E108:0010} Whether I like it or not.

April 2
{E20D}Edgeworth and Co. Law Offices
...Hey, Gregory.
Sorry for reporting in so late.
It may have taken eighteen years...

...but we're finally in a position to prove Samson's
innocence...!

All thanks to your boy, Miles...{E108:0018}
{E107:0003}I couldn't have done it without him.

You should've seen him.{E108:0010} The way he fought for the
truth gave me chills.{E108:0010} It was like I was watching you.

Look,{E108:0010} I know I'm not half the attorney you were...{E108:0010} but
those guiding principles you tried to instill in me?

I like to think I'm embodying them now as I carry on
your legacy.
Here's hoping...
...your boy will be joining me in that soon.
